tools.name: Docker Desktop
tools.desc: Run Docker applications on Windows, Mac, and Linux
pros: Ready to use out of the box, no local install or maintenance
Supports local / Docker deployment, better data privacy
Free tier available, try before you upgrade
cons: Advanced features and higher limits usually require a paid plan
usage:
Step: Open the official site and sign up
Click the red "Visit official site" button to open the Docker Desktop homepage. Find "Sign Up" and log in with email or Google/GitHub.
Tip:
If the site won’t load, check your connection or try another browser.

Step: Pick the plan that fits you
New users usually get a free trial or free quota. Start with the Free tier before upgrading.
Check:
After sign-up you should see the Dashboard home.

Step: Create your first task / project
Click "New" or "Create New" and follow the guide. Pick the first template to start.
Tip:
Don’t start with a complex request. Test with one simple sentence, e.g. "Summarize this page into 3 points".

Step: Review and save the result
When done, the tool shows the result. Export, copy the link, or save locally.
Check:
If unhappy, click "Regenerate" or tweak the prompt and try again.
tools.detail: Docker Desktop is a powerful tool designed for developers to run Docker applications on Windows, Mac, and Linux. It provides a user-friendly interface that simplifies the process of creating, running, and managing containers. Key features include the ability to build and share containerized applications, manage container images, and deploy applications across different environments. It supports Docker Compose for defining and running multi-container applications, and Docker Swarm for orchestrating containerized services. Docker Desktop is ideal for developers who need a comprehensive solution for containerization and orchestration. Pros include its ease of use, robust feature set, and cross-platform compatibility. Limitations may include a learning curve for new users and potential performance issues on less powerful hardware.

tools.detail: Portainer is a lightweight management UI for Docker, designed to simplify the management of Docker containers, images, and networks. It provides a web interface that allows users to easily manage their Docker environment without the need for command-line tools. Key features include container monitoring, image management, and network configuration. Portainer is particularly useful for those who prefer a graphical interface over the command line. It is suitable for both beginners and experienced users. Pros include its simplicity, ease of use, and the ability to manage multiple Docker environments from a single dashboard. Limitations may include limited advanced features compared to other management tools and potential performance issues with large-scale deployments.

tools.detail: Docker Hub is a container registry service provided by Docker, Inc. It serves as a central repository for storing, sharing, and managing container images. Users can search for, download, and upload images to Docker Hub. Key features include image search, versioning, and tagging. It also supports private repositories for secure image storage. Docker Hub is essential for developers who need to collaborate on containerized applications or distribute their own images. Pros include its vast image repository, user-friendly interface, and robust security features. Limitations may include potential performance issues during peak usage times and limitations on the number of private repositories for free accounts.

tools.detail: Docker Compose is a tool for defining and running multi-container Docker applications. It uses YAML files to configure services, networks, and volumes, making it easy to manage complex applications. Key features include service discovery, dependency management, and rolling updates. Docker Compose is particularly useful for developers who need to orchestrate multiple containers as a single service. It is well-suited for both small and large applications. tools.name: Docker Bench for Security
tools.desc: Automated security testing tool for Docker
pros: Free and open source, transparent code, self-hostable for full data control
Supports local / Docker deployment, better data privacy
Free version available, zero cost for personal use
cons: Requires some technical skill to deploy and configure
usage:
Step: Check your environment
This tool runs locally. First make sure your computer meets the basics.
Tip:
Docker Desktop is required.
Check:
Open a terminal and type `docker --version`. If you see a version number, your environment is OK.

Step: Download the code to your machine
Open a terminal in a folder you like and run the commands below:
Code:
git clone https://github.com/docker/docker-bench-for-security.git
cd docker-bench-for-security
Tip:
New to git? If it says command not found, download it from https://git-scm.com.

Step: Install dependencies
The project needs some extra building blocks to run.
Code:
docker build -t {{name}} .
Tip:
If a command errors, it is usually a network issue. Python users can try a mirror.

Step: Fill in the API Key / account config
Many AI tools need a model connection. Find the config item in the README and fill it in.
Code:
# Example: replace xxx with your real Key
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-xxx"
Tip:
Do not screenshot your Key in public groups. Get a free/cheap Key (e.g. GLM-4, DeepSeek) to practice.

Step: Start and run your first task
Run the example command from the project and watch the terminal output.
Code:
docker run -it --rm {{name}}
Check:
If the program prints results (no red Error text), you have it working.

Step: Troubleshooting
Failing the first local deploy is normal. Common issues:
1. Dependency version mismatch → use the Python/Node version the repo recommends;
2. Key not working → check your environment variables;
3. Cannot reach the model API → switch mirror or provider.
Tip:
See more examples in "Related tutorials" below, or click "Visit official site".
tools.detail: Docker Bench for Security is an automated security testing tool designed to help users secure their Docker containers. It scans for common security issues and provides recommendations for improving the security of Docker images and containers. Key features include vulnerability scanning, configuration auditing, and compliance checking. Docker Bench for Security is ideal for organizations that need to ensure the security of their containerized applications. Pros include its automated nature, comprehensive scanning capabilities, and ease of use. Limitations may include a potential false positive rate and the need for manual intervention to address some security issues.
